description: Requires a TechFabric engineer's Microsoft sign-in (scope blog.write). A read, about a millisecond, free: an outline (title options, the opening's two sentences, four to six sections with a line each, the diagram, the FAQ questions; a case study's four sections) against the title, opening, heading and FAQ rules, before any prose; the opening's device and first words are held to the last ten published posts (editorial/voices-of-techfabric.md). Fix what it finds and call again until ready; then show the engineer outline_markdown and draft only after their OK.

diagram.description: What the diagram draws, step by step, and its point. Not for a case study.

faqs.description: Three or more questions a reader would search for. Not for a case study.

meta_title.description: A search title of 60 characters or fewer, only when a title runs longer.

opening.description: The opening's first two sentences: the way this story opens (a device the last ten posts left free: editorial/voices-of-techfabric.md), with one concrete detail and TechFabric doing the work by the second sentence. Not for a case study.

post_type.description: The post type, which sets the opening rule and how hard the fact-check reads it. story (the default): work someone at TechFabric did. The opening has TechFabric doing that work by paragraph two, and every claim gets the full fact-check. perspective: a talk or conference the author attended, a conversation with an industry leader, others' work, or our view of what's possible. TechFabric's view by paragraph two ("we think", "we'd", "I believe" count). What a speaker or another company said is attributed in the sentence ("In her demo, ...") and must match what the author provided; forward-looking views need no source. whats-new: a new feature in AI, Databricks or related tech, and how it could help future projects. Open on what changed (its date and source), then our view. Product facts (name, preview or GA, date, what it does) are checked against the vendor's docs or release notes; forward-looking views need no source. personal: the author's own essay or position, in the first person, about where the work or the industry is going and what people should do. Opening and fact-check as perspective, and the only type that may say "I believe", address the reader as "you", bold up to three thesis sentences, make one "this is not X" thesis reframe and close on a call to act. Never for an engineer explaining a feature or their own project. Choose personal only when the engineer writes in their own voice about a position, never for an engineer explaining a feature or their project. Left out, it is story; an explainer is always whats-new. Not for a case study.

sections.description: Four to six for a post; Challenge, Strategy, Solution and Results for a case study. The FAQ isn't one of them.

summary.description: One line: what the section tells the reader

titles.description: Two or three title options, each one clause naming the subject.

unattended.description: true in a scheduled run with nobody to approve the outline: a passing outline goes straight to drafting.

name: check_outline

outline_markdown.description: The outline as Markdown: show it to the engineer for their OK

post_type.description: The post type the outline was checked as (story when none was sent). Not for a case study

voice.description: How every sentence is said (editorial/voices-of-techfabric.md, "Before you write a sentence"): follow it in the outline, the draft and every rewrite.

title: Check an outline
